verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is scheduled for April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "set to launch no earlier than 6:24 p.m. ET today, Wednesday, April 1, 2026" (R2); "Wednesday, April 1" (R1); "set to launch no earlier than 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 2026" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the launch date as April 1, 2026, matching the claim's month and year.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch occurs at Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "lift off from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R1); "launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R2); "lift off from Kennedy Space Center" (R3); "from Kennedy Space Center" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state Kennedy Space Center as the launch site for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is expected to be visible from parts of Florida, Georgia, and as far north as South Carolina, weather permitting.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "may be visible across most of Florida and into parts of Georgia... Pending weather conditions and cloud cover" (R2); "could be visible for most of Florida to parts of Georgia... past launches... to Myrtle Beach" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly support visibility across Florida and parts of Georgia weather permitting; South Carolina mentioned only for past launches, not explicitly expected for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex offers prime, close-up views of the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex offers the closest public viewing of launches" (R4); "watch from behind NASA’s gates, complete with live commentary... Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as the closest public viewing location for KSC launches, directly applicable to Artemis II.

verifications.claim: Space View Park in Titusville offers prime, close-up views of the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Space View Park: 8 Broad Street, Titusville (parking nearby)" as primary viewing location (R4); "Space View Park in Titusville... ideal Artemis 1 launch-viewing spots" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Listed as a primary/ideal viewing park for Space Coast launches; applicable to Artemis II despite R5 specifying Artemis 1.

verifications.claim: Jetty Park in Cape Canaveral offers prime, close-up views of the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Jetty Park: East end of Port Canaveral off George King Blvd." as viewing location (R4); "Jetty Park in Cape Canaveral... ideal Artemis 1 launch-viewing spots" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Listed as a primary/ideal viewing park for Space Coast launches; applicable to Artemis II despite R5 specifying Artemis 1.

verifications.claim: Residents and visitors across Florida, including Orlando and as far south as West Palm Beach, should be able to see the Artemis II rocket ascend.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Space Coast, Orlando... West Palm Beach" (R2); "Orlando... West Palm Beach... most of Florida" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Visibility maps explicitly include Orlando and West Palm Beach across Florida.

verifications.claim: NASA+ is NASA's free streaming service available on website or app.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA+ ... available to watch through NASA+ on desktop... mobile app on smartphones" (R2); "NASA+ for live coverage... NASA App" (R4); "NASA+, the agency's ad-free, on-demand streaming service, requires no subscription... iOS, Android, web browsers" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm NASA+ as free, accessible via website, app, no subscription.

verifications.claim: NASA's official YouTube channel provides full coverage of the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA is also broadcasting the launch attempt live on its YouTube channel" (R1); "NASA+ ... from its official site and YouTube" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm live coverage on NASA's YouTube channel.

verifications.claim: Amazon Prime Video streams the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA content, including... the highly anticipated Artemis II mission... available... through Prime Video... one of Prime Video's FAST channels" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states Artemis II mission available on Prime Video without subscription.

verifications.claim: NBC News NOW streams the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "tuning into ​​​​​NBC News NOW... to see... the Artemis II launch... 24/7 streaming network" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of NBC News NOW streaming the Artemis II launch.

verifications.claim: FOX Weather streams the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: R5 mentions FOX Weather for Artemis 1 launch only; no sources mention streaming Artemis II.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launch dates and times are subject to change.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If the launch is postponed, there are two other windows" (R1); "with a two-hour window" (R2); "dates and times are always subject to change with little notice" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources note launch windows, potential postponements, and explicit statements on changes.
